title: Music shows an instructor's whole library song list, and library search reaches all of it
acceptance: Liked or library songs are not cut off at 200 for Apple Music, Spotify or SoundCloud: the list pages (a "Load more" or incremental load), or loads the full set within a documented upper bound that says when it is reached.
Search on the Songs list finds a song that sits past the first page, either by loading it or by a server-side search.
"Create class from liked songs" uses the same paging and says when it used a subset.
The "Recents" sort is relabeled or reimplemented: today it is the provider's own order (alphabetical for Apple library songs), not recency.
GET /providers/:provider/likes changes are registered in generate-openapi.ts and the OpenAPI drift and contract-parity checks pass; the iOS snapshot refresh is a separate iOS PR.
No provider audio or derived data is cached; any paging cursor is the provider's own.
nextAction: Plan first: choose client paging vs server search per provider (Apple, Spotify and SoundCloud expose different library APIs) and re-verify each provider API before coding. Files: packages/music/src/{apple-music,spotify,soundcloud}.ts, apps/api/src/lib/music/user-likes.ts, apps/api/src/routes/providers.ts, apps/web Music workspace. Owner-gated (provider code): the PR needs owner-approved. Surface: both (API contract).

evidence.summary: fetchAppleMusicLibrarySongs defaults maxTracks to 200 (pages of 100); spotify.ts and soundcloud.ts use the same default. user-likes.ts never passes maxTracks; the /likes route takes no cursor. Checked on main c9b89a7.
filterLibrary filters only the loaded rows; orderLibrary returns provider order for "recents". Checked on main c9b89a7.
2026-10-28 owner UX audit of production: Top priority 1 (P0) and Music rows on the 200-song cap, search and Recents. Browser evidence; not re-observed at intake.
